intended_object: The standard ℤ-basis (e_0, …, e_r) of the standard lattice ℤ^{r+1} ⊂ ℚ^{r+1}, the lattice spanned by the coordinate vectors in the standard representation of sl_{r+1}. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation ("the standard admissible lattice and its coordinate basis") and the lemma `coe_latticeBasis`.
explanation:
The definition is the library's general `TauCeti.coordinateLatticeBasis` specialised to the index type `Fin (r + 1)`. That general basis is `(Pi.basisFun ℚ ι).restrictScalars ℤ`, a basis over ℤ of the ℤ-span of the standard basis vectors of ι → ℚ. The lemma `coe_latticeBasis` shows that the i-th basis vector is `Pi.single i 1`, which is exactly the standard coordinate basis of ℤ^{r+1}.

The target type is written as `(lattice r).toAddSubgroup`. As the docstring says, its carrier and ℤ-module structure are definitionally those of the submodule, and the file compiles, so this is only a matter of presentation.

The restriction to `Fin (r + 1)` is not too narrow. This is a specific object in the sl_{r+1} setup of this file, and the general version for any index type already exists in the library as `TauCeti.coordinateLatticeBasis`. Mathlib has no separate named "coordinate lattice basis"; the closest Mathlib construction is `Module.Basis.restrictScalars` applied to `Pi.basisFun`, which the library uses directly. There is no discrepancy, so the verdict is faithful.
